tour.overview:
North of Cairns, the Daintree is part of the oldest continuously surviving tropical rainforest on Earth, estimated at well over 100 million years old, and part of the Wet Tropics World Heritage Area. At Cape Tribulation, named by Captain Cook in 1770 after his ship struck the reef, the forest runs down to white beaches facing the Great Barrier Reef. It is the traditional country of the Eastern Kuku Yalanji people.

This private day takes you there with a local guide and a car, with an indigenous-guided walk, a crocodile cruise and the boardwalks and beaches of the Daintree coast.

AT A GLANCE
• Duration: about 9 hours
• Start and end: your hotel in Cairns or Port Douglas
• Type: private tour with local guide, car and driver
• Booking: on request – we confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay only then
• Level: easy

WHAT YOU SEE
• Mossman Gorge.
• The Daintree River.
• Rainforest boardwalks.
• Cape Tribulation.

WHY THIS WORKS
Your guide knows where to look for crocodiles, cassowaries and tree kangaroos, and the private car lets you linger on the beaches.

WHO IT SUITS
Nature lovers, families, photographers.

WHO MAY PREFER ANOTHER TOUR
For the reef itself, choose our Great Barrier Reef day.

PRACTICAL INFORMATION
Do not swim in the rivers or, from November to May, unprotected sea: crocodiles and stingers. Bring insect repellent.

days.name: Mossman Gorge, a Daintree River crocodile cruise, the rainforest and Cape Tribulation
days.description:
What to expect: the rainforest, its wildlife and its coast, with a local guide, private car, cruise, walk and lunch.

Your guide and driver collect you in the morning and drive north along the Captain Cook Highway, a coastal road of beaches and headlands. At Mossman Gorge, a Kuku Yalanji guide leads you on a Dreamtime walk through the rainforest, explaining bush foods, medicines and traditional stories, ending with a smoking ceremony. You also see the clear river tumbling over granite boulders.

On the Daintree River, a small boat takes you in search of estuarine crocodiles basking on the mud banks, along with tree snakes and kingfishers. You cross the river on the cable ferry into the Daintree National Park, and walk boardwalks through the forest of fan palms, strangler figs and ancient ferns at Jindalba or Marrdja, watching for the endangered southern cassowary.

Lunch is in the rainforest, followed by Cape Tribulation, where the forest meets a long white beach. On the way back, you stop for ice cream made from rainforest fruits such as soursop and black sapote, and at the Alexandra Range lookout over the Daintree River mouth.

SCHEDULE (approximate times)
07:30 – Pick-up in Cairns or 08:30 in Port Douglas.
09:30 – Mossman Gorge Dreamtime walk.
11:15 – Daintree River cruise.
12:30 – Daintree ferry and rainforest boardwalk.
13:30 – Lunch.
14:30 – Cape Tribulation.
15:45 – Ice cream and the lookout.
17:30 – Back at your hotel.

GOOD TO KNOW
• Sightings of cassowaries are rare but possible; never approach them.
• Port Douglas is a good base, closer to the Daintree.

INCLUDED: private car and driver, local guide, Dreamtime walk, river cruise, ferry, lunch, bottled water.
NOT INCLUDED: drinks, tips.

Overnight: none.
Meals: lunch.

faq.question: How does booking on request work?
faq.answer: You choose a date and the number of travellers and send the request. Nothing is charged. We confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay online only when the tour is confirmed.

faq.question: Will we see crocodiles?
faq.answer: Very likely, especially in the cooler months when they bask on the banks. They are wild, so sightings are never guaranteed.

faq.question: Can we swim?
faq.answer: Not in the rivers or creeks near the coast, because of crocodiles. Mossman Gorge has a swimming spot when conditions allow.

faq.question: Is it suitable for children?
faq.answer: Yes. Children love the crocodiles and the boardwalks. Child seats are provided free of charge on request.

faq.question: Is it suitable for people with limited mobility?
faq.answer: Largely. The boardwalks are flat; the river boat needs a step.

faq.question: Can we combine it with the reef?
faq.answer: Yes, on another day; or with a 2-day stay at a rainforest lodge.

faq.question: Are there many mosquitoes?
faq.answer: Some, especially in the wet season. Bring repellent.

faq.question: What about the wet season?
faq.answer: From January to March, heavy rain may change the route; the forest is at its most lush.

faq.question: What should we wear?
faq.answer: Light clothes, a hat, closed walking shoes, insect repellent and sun cream.

faq.question: What is the best time of year?
faq.answer: May to October is drier and cooler.

faq.question: Should we tip?
faq.answer: Tipping is not expected in Australia, where wages are higher, but it is always appreciated for excellent service.

faq.question: What is the cancellation policy?
faq.answer: You can cancel free of charge up to 24 hours before the tour. Until your request is confirmed, nothing is charged at all.
